approachQuestion.prompt:
List shared shipment labels

Input: arrays dispatch and received. Return each distinct label present in both arrays exactly once, in the order of its first occurrence in dispatch.

Example 1: dispatch = [8,3,8,2,3], received = [3,8,8]. Output: [8,3]. Example 2: dispatch = [1,1], received = [2]. Output: []. Example 3: dispatch = [], received = [4]. Output: []. Both lengths are between 0 and 200,000.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Build a set from received. Scan dispatch in order; if its label is in the set, append it and remove it from that set.
options.feedback: The first successful occurrence emits the label at the required position; removal prevents all later copies from emitting it again.

options.text: Build a membership set from received and an initially empty emitted set. Scan dispatch and append a label only if it is received and not emitted, then mark it emitted.
options.feedback: The extra emitted set enforces the same invariant with the same expected growth in time and auxiliary space.

options.text: For each dispatch occurrence, scan all of received for membership and scan the current output before appending to avoid duplicates.
options.feedback: This is correct but brute force: repeated membership and output scans are avoidable.

options.text: Build a set of received and append every dispatch entry whose value belongs to it.
options.feedback: dispatch [1,1] and received [1] would produce [1,1] rather than [1].

feedback.reason: Distinguish membership from multiplicity and suppress output duplicates without losing source order.
details: Build a mutable set of received labels, then scan dispatch. Append a present label to output and remove it from the set immediately. Do not copy dispatch.
Deleting a label after emitting it suppresses later dispatch duplicates. Scanning dispatch preserves its order; sorting or iterating only the received set would discard that ordering rule.

“Build a set from received. Scan dispatch in order; if its label is in the set, append it and remove it from that set.”: The first successful occurrence emits the label at the required position; removal prevents all later copies from emitting it again.

“Build a membership set from received and an initially empty emitted set. Scan dispatch and append a label only if it is received and not emitted, then mark it emitted.”: The extra emitted set enforces the same invariant with the same expected growth in time and auxiliary space.

“For each dispatch occurrence, scan all of received for membership and scan the current output before appending to avoid duplicates.”: This is correct but brute force: repeated membership and output scans are avoidable.
“Build a set of received and append every dispatch entry whose value belongs to it.”: dispatch [1,1] and received [1] would produce [1,1] rather than [1].

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “List shared shipment labels — analyzed method”, n = dispatch.length, m = received.length and u is the number of distinct labels in received. Output append has amortized constant cost. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + m + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.
Expected O(n + m + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Build one membership set and scan dispatch once.
details: Distinguish membership from multiplicity and suppress output duplicates without losing source order.
The method inserts m received entries and checks n dispatch entries, with at most one removal per emitted label. Expected O(n+m+1); appending the result costs at most O(n).
The only non-result collection is the set of u distinct received labels. Constant scalar and call-stack storage gives O(u+1).
“Expected O(n + m + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + m + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space.”: The received membership set retains up to u labels.
“O(nm + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: Hash membership avoids a full received scan per dispatch entry.
“O((n+m) log(n+m) + 1) time; O(n+m+1) space.”: The analyzed method neither sorts nor copies both arrays.
